## NFL injury briefing

### Key new injury statuses
- **Steelers WR Cole Burgess** — carted off after an apparent **lower-body injury** during 7-on-7s in Pittsburgh’s first padded practice.
- **Panthers WR Xavier Legette** — carted off Tuesday with an **upper-body injury**.
- **Bears RB Kyle Monangai** — **day to day** with a **soft tissue injury**, per coach Ben Johnson.
- **Cowboys TE Princeton Fant** — left practice on a cart with a **knee injury** and is scheduled for an **MRI**.
- **49ers rookie DE Mikail Kamara** — **tore his ACL** at practice.
- **Broncos C Luke Wattenberg** — left practice early with an **apparent injury**; backup **Alex Forsyth** took first-team reps.
- **Coby Bryant** — carted off practice after grabbing his **knee**; one report says he is expected to **miss 8-10 weeks**.

### Returning from injury
- **Colts QB Daniel Jones** — eight months removed from an **Achilles tear**, and he has taken **every first-team rep** through four camp practices. He reportedly looks good moving.

### Why it matters
- **Legette** and **Monangai** are the biggest immediate fantasy watch items because their availability could shift quickly in camp.
- **Kamara’s ACL tear** is a major long-term loss for San Francisco’s defensive depth.
- **Jones’ camp usage** suggests Indianapolis is giving him a full runway as the starter, which matters for the Colts offense and any fantasy investment there.
- **Wattenberg’s status** could affect Denver’s interior line if the injury lingers.

### What to watch next
- MRI results for **Princeton Fant**.
- Updates on the severity of **Xavier Legette’s** upper-body injury.
- Whether **Kyle Monangai** gets back on the field quickly.
- Any confirmation on **Coby Bryant’s** timetable beyond the 8-10 week report.

- **Drake Maye (QB)** — The second-year QB said he looks more comfortable in Josh McDaniels’ offense and has “more on his plate” than last season. That’s a clear scheme/usage step forward and points to a higher fantasy ceiling if the added command translates to more efficient production. [5]

- **Romeo Doubs (WR)** — Doubs has worked as the Patriots’ top slot option, with some snaps split out wide, and he added a Monday touchdown against Christian Gonzalez. He’s not just in the mix; he has a defined role in a crowded room, which keeps him in the weekly target conversation. [2, 9]

- **DeMario Douglas (WR)** — Maye called Douglas “the slot” and said he’s a big piece for New England in 11 personnel, with his route chemistry continuing to improve. That locks in a usage-driven role that matters for short-area targets and PPR value. [2]

- **Kyle Williams (WR)** — Maye said Williams is working to expand his route tree in Year 2 while still bringing clear deep speed. If that growth sticks, Williams could become more than a one-trick vertical threat and earn more consistent snaps. [2]

He’s just one of those guys that is quiet, does everything the right way, cares about his teammates, and he just puts his head down and works.
